open_obligations: Check whether the COVID-19 task has an information asymmetry like Khan et al.'s debates.
Check which LLM judges Khan et al. compare with humans.
Check whether persona conditioning is a fair comparison with unconditioned human judges.
in.other_title: Persona-conditioned LLM judges of debate reach 78.5% and 77.3% vs 70.1% for human judges
in.rationale: Khan et al. report that across all protocols humans have higher judge accuracy than LLM judges. Rahman et al. report default GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-7B debate judges are comparable to humans (69.8% and 70.7% vs 70.1%) and persona-based GPT-4o judges exceed them (up to 78.5%) on COVID-19 claims; the cited Khan et al. passage does not name its task or its LLM judges, and only it describes its debates as information-asymmetric.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether human judges of AI debate are more accurate than LLM judges

open_obligations: Note that Michael et al.'s AI consultants were much worse at arguing convincingly for the wrong answer; check which model Khan et al.'s consultants use and how strong they are.
Check the size of Khan et al.'s incorrect-consultant accuracy drop, and whether it is reported for human judges, LLM judges or both.
Check that judge interaction is allowed in both consultancy setups.
out.other_title: Dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time; judges do better against dishonest AI ones
out.rationale: Michael et al. report dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time on QuALITY-hard. Khan et al. report that in consultancy incorrect experts cause low judge accuracy, suggesting it is easier to be misled in consultancy. Michael et al. also found judges reach 87% accuracy with dishonest AI consultants, which they explain at least in part by their AIs being much worse at arguing convincingly for the wrong answer, so the support comes from Michael et al.'s human consultants rather than their AI consultants.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether dishonest consultants mislead human judges in hidden-passage QuALITY consultancy

text: The paper reports that in consultancy, incorrect experts cause low judge accuracy, suggesting it is easier to be misled in consultancy, and that across all protocols humans have higher judge accuracy than LLM judges. It finds identical judge accuracy between static and interactive debate and says this suggests that adding non-expert interaction does not help in information-asymmetric debates, which the authors call surprising.
title: Judge interaction does not raise debate accuracy; incorrect consultants mislead
